response.title: Can I charge a power station from solar panels in an unheated garage or shed when it's below freezing?
response.answer:
Yes, you can connect solar panels to a portable power station in an unheated garage or shed during freezing weather—but whether it's safe to charge depends on the battery's temperature and its built-in protection system.

The biggest concern is that most portable power stations use lithium-ion batteries, which generally should not be charged below 32°F (0°C) unless the manufacturer specifically permits it.

What happens below freezing?

Battery temperature

	

Charging recommendation




Above 41°F (5°C)

	

Generally safe within manufacturer limits




32–41°F (0–5°C)

	

Usually allowed, sometimes at reduced rates




Below 32°F (0°C)

	

Do not charge unless specifically supported




Below 14°F (-10°C)

	

Charging is generally prohibited without battery heating or specialized technology

Charging a cold lithium battery can cause lithium plating, which permanently damages battery cells and can increase safety risks.

This applies to both common power station chemistries: LiFePO4 (LFP) and NMC.

What about solar charging?

Solar panels themselves work well in cold weather. In fact, solar cells can become more efficient as temperatures decrease.

The issue is the battery inside the power station, not the solar panels.

For example, if your shed is 20°F (-7°C) and sunlight reaches your solar panels, the panels can produce electricity, but your power station may refuse to accept it until its battery warms up.

How to make it work safely in winter

There are three practical approaches:

Use a power station with built-in battery heating. Some models can use incoming solar energy to warm the battery before charging. EcoFlow documents this capability on certain LFP battery systems. 
EcoFlow US
+1

Keep the power station in a warmer location. Put the solar panels outside and run a properly rated solar cable to the power station indoors. This is often the simplest solution.

Use a temperature-controlled, insulated enclosure. A purpose-built battery enclosure with thermostatic heating can work in a shed, provided it maintains safe temperatures and preserves the power station's required ventilation and clearances.

Also, check the solar panels' maximum open-circuit voltage in freezing weather. Cold weather increases panel voltage, potentially exceeding the power station's solar input limit.

Does the power station automatically protect itself?

Many modern units have a battery management system (BMS) that stops charging when the battery is too cold. For example, the EcoFlow E980 specifies a minimum charging temperature of 32°F and includes low-temperature protection. 
EcoFlow Manuals
+1

However, you should not assume every model has adequate protection.

One question: What brand and model of power station are you using or considering? For example, EcoFlow DELTA 2, Jackery Explorer 1000 v2, or BLUETTI AC180.

I can tell you whether that specific model can safely stay connected to solar panels all winter in an unheated shed, including whether it automatically resumes charging when temperatures rise.
